To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
prostasin is a serine protease with anti‐metastatic activity that is transcriptionally regulated via promoter DNA methylation in breast cancer cells.
prostasin is a novel inhibitor of breast cancer cell invasiveness that is regulated by promoter DNA hypermethylation.
prostasin is expressed in normal human breast epithelial cells and in nonmetastatic, noninvasive breast carcinoma cell lines, but absent in metastatic, highly invasive breast carcinoma cell lines.

the identification of genes that regulate prostate and breast cancer invasivity and metastatic potential.

the role of prostasin serine proteinase in breast cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
prostasin is a novel serine protease that may be a useful biomarker in prostate cancer.
prostasin is a novel gene that is regulated by methylation in the breast.

prostasin is a novel tumor suppressor gene for prostate cancer, that is, the loss of its expression correlates with tumor progression and its expression is associated with decreased invasiveness and growth of prostate cancer cells in vivo.

prostasin expression is downregulated in highly invasive breast cancer cells by promoter methylation and reexpression of prostatin in highly invasive breast cells reduces their invasiveness in vitro.
